library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

```{r meta}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Savic_2017_rifapentine"))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: [doi:10.1002/cpt.634](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.634)

Savic 2017 pooled the rifapentine arms of two phase II tuberculosis treatment
trials (TB Trials Consortium Studies 29 and 29X) to find the rifapentine dose
with the greatest treatment-shortening potential. The analysis had two layers:

1. a joint population PK model for rifapentine and its active metabolite
   25-O-desacetyl rifapentine (Table 2), packaged here; and
2. Weibull time-to-event models for stable sputum culture conversion driven by
   the individual rifapentine AUC0-24, which are **not** packaged (see
   Assumptions and deviations).

The PK model is a one-compartment model with first-order absorption for the
parent. All parent elimination forms the metabolite, which has its own
one-compartment disposition (Supplementary Figure S1). Because the fraction
metabolised cannot be identified from plasma data, the metabolite clearance and
volume are apparent values (CLm/Fm, Vm/Fm). The paper's reference condition is a
450 mg dose taken with a high-fat meal by a 31-year-old Black man without HIV
infection.

# Population

`r mod$population$n_subjects` adults with smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis
received rifapentine during the 8-week intensive phase (Savic 2017 Table 1):
median age 31 years, median weight 55 kg, 71% men, 60% Black, 19% White, 16%
Asian, and 9% HIV-infected. Study 29 gave 10 mg/kg rifapentine 5 days a week
fasting; Study 29X gave 10, 15 or 20 mg/kg 7 days a week with food. Doses were
given as 150 mg tablets, so the absolute doses were 450 to 1500 mg. 2203
rifapentine and metabolite concentrations were collected between weeks 2 and 8,
by sparse (1-3 samples) or intensive (7 samples) sampling.

```{r population}
str(mod$population)
```

# Typical-value steady state

Each typical subject is a 31-year-old Black man without HIV infection; the
rows vary dose and meal. Fourteen once-daily doses are given and the
14th dosing interval (312-336 h) is analysed, which is at steady state (the
slowest rate constant, `ka = 0.07 1/h`, has a 9.9 h half-life).

The model has two error endpoints, so every observation row names one with
`dvid`; both concentrations come back as columns.

```{r typical-events}
tau <- 24
n_dose <- 14L
t_last <- (n_dose - 1L) * tau
obs_times <- seq(t_last, t_last + tau, by = 0.25)

ref_cov <- list(
  AGE = 31, SEXF = 0, RACE_WHITE = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0, HIV_POS = 0
)

typ_subj <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,              ~dose, ~FED_HIGHFAT, ~FED_LOWFAT,
  "450 mg, high-fat",        450,            1,           0,
  "600 mg, high-fat",        600,            1,           0,
  "900 mg, high-fat",        900,            1,           0,
  "1200 mg, high-fat",      1200,            1,           0,
  "1200 mg, low-fat",       1200,            0,           1,
  "1200 mg, fasting",       1200,            0,           0
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), !!!ref_cov)

make_events <- function(subj) {
  doses <- subj |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      id, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_,
      ii = tau, addl = n_dose - 1L
    )
  obs <- subj |>
    dplyr::select(id) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L,
      ii = NA_real_, addl = NA_integer_
    )
  covs <- subj |>
    dplyr::select(
      id, AGE, SEXF, RACE_WHITE, RACE_ASIAN, HIV_POS, FED_HIGHFAT, FED_LOWFAT,
      DOSE_RIFAPENTINE_MG = dose
    )
  # Event columns first, covariates after them.
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(covs, by = "id")
}

typ_events <- make_events(typ_subj)
```

```{r typical-solve}
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = typ_events,
  omega = NA,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(typ_subj, id, treatment), by = "id")

stopifnot(
  nrow(sim_typ) > 0,
  !anyNA(sim_typ$Cc), !anyNA(sim_typ$Cc_desrpt),
  # random effects are off: one clearance value per typical subject
  all(tapply(sim_typ$cl, sim_typ$id, function(x) length(unique(round(x, 10)))) == 1L)
)
```

```{r typical-profiles, fig.cap = "Typical steady-state profiles over one dosing interval for rifapentine and 25-O-desacetyl rifapentine (31-year-old Black man without HIV infection)."}
sim_typ |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, time, Rifapentine = Cc, `Desacetyl rifapentine` = Cc_desrpt) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(treatment, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    tad = time - t_last,
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = typ_subj$treatment)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, conc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ug/mL)", colour = NULL)
```

## PKNCA against the closed-form steady-state exposure

At steady state the parent AUC over one dosing interval is `F * Dose / CL`.
Every eliminated parent molecule becomes metabolite, so the metabolite
AUC over the interval is `Fm * F * Dose / CLm` on the apparent scale. Both
sides use the same parameter values, so this checks the encoding (dose-level
and meal factors, the Fm switch, units) rather than the paper.

```{r typical-pknca}
run_nca <- function(sim, conc_col, events, subj) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    dplyr::transmute(id, time, conc = .data[[conc_col]], treatment)
  dose <- subj |>
    dplyr::transmute(id, time = t_last, amt = dose, treatment)
  stopifnot(all(c(t_last, t_last + tau) %in% conc$time))
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "ug/mL", timeu = "h"),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
    intervals = data.frame(
      start = t_last, end = t_last + tau,
      cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
    )
  ))
  as.data.frame(res$result)
}

nca_parent <- run_nca(sim_typ, "Cc", typ_events, typ_subj)
nca_metab <- run_nca(sim_typ, "Cc_desrpt", typ_events, typ_subj)

f_dose <- function(dose) {
  dplyr::case_when(dose <= 450 ~ 1, dose <= 600 ~ 0.91, dose <= 900 ~ 0.83, TRUE ~ 0.74)
}
closed <- typ_subj |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    f = f_dose(dose) * ifelse(FED_LOWFAT == 1, 0.83, 1) *
      ifelse(FED_HIGHFAT == 0 & FED_LOWFAT == 0, 0.72, 1),
    fm = ifelse(dose > 600, 1.34, 1),
    auc_parent = f * dose / 1.86,
    auc_metab = fm * f * dose / 1.91
  )

cmp_parent <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_parent,
  reference = closed |> dplyr::select(treatment, auclast = auc_parent),
  by = "treatment",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 1
)
knitr::kable(cmp_parent, caption = "Rifapentine AUC0-24 at steady state: PKNCA on the packaged model (Simulated) against F * Dose / CL from Savic 2017 Table 2 (Reference).")

cmp_metab <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_metab,
  reference = closed |> dplyr::select(treatment, auclast = auc_metab),
  by = "treatment",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 1
)
knitr::kable(cmp_metab, caption = "Desacetyl rifapentine AUC0-24 at steady state: PKNCA (Simulated) against Fm * F * Dose / CLm (Reference).")
```

```{r typical-gate}
gate_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_parent |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
    dplyr::left_join(closed, by = "treatment") |>
    dplyr::transmute(pct = 100 * (PPORRES / auc_parent - 1)),
  nca_metab |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
    dplyr::left_join(closed, by = "treatment") |>
    dplyr::transmute(pct = 100 * (PPORRES / auc_metab - 1))
)
# The two sides share every parameter, so only trapezoid error separates them.
stopifnot(nrow(gate_typ) == 12L, all(abs(gate_typ$pct) < 1))
```

The typical 600 mg steady-state Cmax is
`r round(nca_parent$PPORRES[nca_parent$PPTESTCD == "cmax" & nca_parent$treatment == "600 mg, high-fat"], 1)`
ug/mL, close to the 15.7 ug/mL median of the 211 participants who received
600 mg (Table 3); the typical AUC0-24 of 293 ug h/mL is likewise close to the
Table 3 median of 295 ug h/mL. Table 3 pools both studies, all meal conditions
and the full covariate mix, so this is a plausibility check, not a gate.

# Replicating Figure 3: AUC0-24 by dose and meal

Figure 3 shows the distribution of rifapentine AUC0-24 at 900 and 1200 mg
daily by meal (high fat, lower fat, fasting). Its six medians were read off the
published figure by the maintainers, calibrated against the 300 and
350 ug h/mL reference lines. The virtual cohort draws race, sex, HIV status and
age from the rifapentine column of Table 1, 200 participants per dose and meal
arm.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2017)
n_per_arm <- 200L

draw_age <- function(n) {
  # log-normal around the median age of 31 years, redrawn into 18-70 years
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- round(31 * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)))
    out <- c(out, x[x >= 18 & x <= 70])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

arms <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  dose = c(900, 1200),
  meal = c("high fat", "lower fat", "fasting")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste0(dose, " mg, ", meal))

cohort <- arms |>
  dplyr::slice(rep(seq_len(dplyr::n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    race = sample(c("Black", "White", "Asian", "Other"), dplyr::n(), TRUE,
      prob = c(0.60, 0.19, 0.16, 0.05)
    ),
    RACE_WHITE = as.integer(race == "White"),
    RACE_ASIAN = as.integer(race == "Asian"),
    SEXF = rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.294),
    HIV_POS = rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.09),
    AGE = draw_age(dplyr::n()),
    FED_HIGHFAT = as.integer(meal == "high fat"),
    FED_LOWFAT = as.integer(meal == "lower fat")
  )

coh_events <- make_events(cohort)
sim_coh <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = coh_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, treatment), by = "id")
nca_coh <- run_nca(sim_coh, "Cc", coh_events, cohort)
```

```{r figure3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Savic 2017: simulated steady-state rifapentine AUC0-24 by dose and meal (boxes), with the published medians (red diamonds), the 350 ug h/mL target (green) and the 300 ug h/mL low-exposure line (red)."}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,              ~auclast,
  "900 mg, high fat",       475,
  "900 mg, lower fat",      418,
  "900 mg, fasting",        334,
  "1200 mg, high fat",      570,
  "1200 mg, lower fat",     503,
  "1200 mg, fasting",       398
)

auc_coh <- nca_coh |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = fig3$treatment))

ggplot(auc_coh, aes(treatment, PPORRES)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(
    data = dplyr::mutate(fig3, treatment = factor(treatment, levels = fig3$treatment)),
    aes(y = auclast), colour = "red", shape = 18, size = 4
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 350, colour = "green3") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 300, colour = "red") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1100)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUC0-24 (ug*h/mL)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

```{r figure3-table}
cmp_fig3 <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_coh,
  reference = fig3,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_fig3, caption = "Median steady-state AUC0-24 by dose and meal: virtual cohort (Simulated) against the medians read from Savic 2017 Figure 3 (Reference).")
```

```{r figure3-gate}
gate_fig3 <- auc_coh |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::mutate(fig3, treatment = factor(treatment, levels = fig3$treatment)), by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / auclast - 1))
stopifnot(
  nrow(gate_fig3) == 6L,
  # Centre: a mis-transcribed CL/F, dose-level factor or meal factor moves
  # the medians by tens of percent.
  abs(median(gate_fig3$pct)) < 10,
  # Envelope over six cohort medians whose covariate mix is assumed, not known.
  max(abs(gate_fig3$pct)) < 25
)
```

The ratios between the published medians test the dose-level and meal
factors without any cohort: the 1200/900 mg ratio is 1.20 in Figure 3 against
`0.74 * 1200 / (0.83 * 900) =` `r round(0.74 * 1200 / (0.83 * 900), 3)` in the
model, and the fasting/high-fat ratio is 0.70 against 0.72. The lower-fat
medians in the figure (0.88 of high fat) sit a little above the model's 0.83;
Figure 3 summarises individual estimates of participants who chose each meal,
whose covariate mix differs between groups.

# Between-subject spread of AUC0-24

Supplementary Figure S3 gives the median AUC0-24 with its 5th-95th percentile
range for the narrowest subgroup, Black men under 30 years without HIV:
322 [169, 568] ug h/mL. With race, sex and HIV fixed, the spread of log AUC is
set by the random effects on F and CL/F alone,
`var(log AUC) = omega_F^2 + omega_CL^2 - 2 cov(CL, F)`.

```{r iiv-spread}
om <- mod$omega
sd_log_auc <- sqrt(om["etalfdepot", "etalfdepot"] + om["etalcl", "etalcl"] -
  2 * om["etalcl", "etalfdepot"])
sd_fig_s3 <- log(568 / 169) / (2 * qnorm(0.95))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Source = c("Packaged model (Table 2 IIV)", "Supplementary Figure S3, bottom row"),
    `SD of log AUC0-24` = signif(c(sd_log_auc, sd_fig_s3), 3),
    `95th / 5th percentile ratio` = signif(exp(2 * qnorm(0.95) * c(sd_log_auc, sd_fig_s3)), 3),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
# The figure's subgroup still mixes ages and meals, so it is slightly wider.
stopifnot(abs(sd_log_auc / sd_fig_s3 - 1) < 0.15)
```

The positive CL-F correlation (0.55) cancels much of the two variances: AUC
varies with a log-SD of about 0.35, smaller than either random effect would
suggest on its own.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Culture-conversion models not packaged.** The paper's exposure-response
  layer is a Weibull time-to-event model for stable culture conversion. The
  supplement prints the base parameters (rifapentine scale 0.0137 1/day,
  shape 2.04, AUC50 313 ug h/mL, Emax -0.346; rifampin scale 0.01472 1/day,
  shape 2.115), but not how the Emax term enters the hazard, and not the
  coefficients of the retained covariates (cavity size, African study site,
  Karnofsky score, smear grade, food; Supplementary Table S5 gives P values
  only). Table 4 shows group-specific shapes, so the final model is not the
  printed base model. Without the drug-effect form and the covariate
  coefficients the model cannot be written down, so it is left out. The
  rifampin base parameters do reproduce the 114-day time for 95% of control
  participants quoted in Figure 1 (`(log 20)^(1/2.115) / 0.01472` =
  `r round(log(20)^(1 / 2.115) / 0.01472)` days).
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 gives IIV as CV%; the variances use
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` and each covariance is the Table 2 correlation times the two SDs.
* **Dose bands.** The paper estimated one relative bioavailability per dose
  given (450, 600, 900, and 1200 pooled with 1500 mg). The model reads the dose
  from `DOSE_RIFAPENTINE_MG` and places other doses in the next-higher band
  (for example 750 mg uses the 900 mg factor). Doses below 450 mg use the
  reference. The 1.34-fold Fm effect applies to doses above 600 mg as printed.
* **Meal coding.** The paper's reference meal is high fat (> 27 g fat).
  Fasting is coded as `FED_HIGHFAT = FED_LOWFAT = 0`; the two indicators must
  not both be 1.
* **Race.** Table 2 gives effects for White and Asian race relative to Black.
  The 4% of participants of other or unreported race get no effect, which
  treats them as the reference.
* **Fraction metabolised.** With all parent elimination forming metabolite
  and Fm unidentified, the metabolite clearance and volume are apparent
  values; the dose-dependent Fm factor scales metabolite formation, so above
  600 mg the metabolite amount is not mass-balanced against the parent. No
  molecular-weight correction is applied, as in the paper.
* **AUC variability statement.** The Results describe a 21% CV for AUC0-24,
  which the Table 2 random effects do not reproduce (they imply about 36%);
  Supplementary Figure S3, used above, agrees with Table 2.
* **Virtual cohort.** The age distribution (log-normal around the median of
  31 years, 18-70 years) is assumed; Table 1 gives only the median. Sex, race
  and HIV proportions are those of the rifapentine column of Table 1.
* **Study 29 dosing frequency.** Study 29 gave rifapentine 5 days a week, and
  the paper scaled those participants' AUC by 5/7 for the exposure-response
  analysis only. The PK model itself does not depend on it.
